display.purpose: The wallboard's headline reading. One per screen, sized in viewport units because it is read from four metres away; it drops to clamp(2.75rem, 13vw, 5rem) below lg as the board reflows to a column.

headline.purpose: The wallboard's secondary readings; clamp(2rem, 9vw, 3.5rem) below lg.

title.purpose: Property card titles, rendered as level-3 headings. Small on purpose: it names one card in a grid of thirty, and shouting would defeat scanning.

body.purpose: The default. Almost everything on the panel.

label.purpose: Uppercase group headings, the driver-internals disclosure, the debug detail line. The wallboard's field captions are the same shape one notch wider (+0.1em) and sized in vw.

reading.purpose: Every numeric or wire-derived value: telemetry, log lines, raw INDI names behind the debug toggle. Tabular figures, so a live number never jitters.

shadows.name: xs
shadows.purpose: Inputs and outline buttons. Observed, not prescribed: the system is flat and the scale's purpose is undecided.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Every card. Below the threshold of perception; the hairline border and the surface tone are what actually separate a card from the page.

shadows.name: 2xl
shadows.purpose: The only step in the scale that is visible at all. Unused by the panel.

shadows.name: dark-scale
shadows.purpose: The dark and night schemes run the same ramp at roughly double the alpha, which on a near-black ground is less perceptible still.

motion.name: state-pulse
motion.purpose: The Busy indicator, on [data-indi-pulse]::after. An outline that scales 1 -> 1.5 and fades 0.6 -> 0, so the badge's own contrast is identical at every frame and only transform and opacity animate. An outline paints outside the pseudo-element's box, so no animated pixel touches the label. Declared inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so it does not exist at all for a reader who asked for stillness.

motion.name: accordion
motion.purpose: The driver-internals fold and the docked message strip. Neutralised to 1ms under reduced motion rather than to 0, so Radix Presence still receives animationend and unmounts.

motion.name: reduced-motion-whitelist
motion.value: transition-property: color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, box-shadow, opacity
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the system narrows transitions to this list rather than killing them. The blanket animation-duration override is deliberately not used: it takes the focus ring's transition with it, and the ring is an accessibility affordance rather than decoration.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: A filled neutral, not a brand colour. Sparingly is an understatement: nothing on the panel's own surface is one. It appears inside DeviceConfigDialog and nowhere else, because a filled control marks the action of a surface an operator opened deliberately, and a screen of live instrument readings has no such action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--primary, #12151a); color: var(--primary-foreground, #ffffff); font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, #12151a) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, #fbfcfd), 0 0 0 5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #0a0c0f) 75%, transparent); border-color: var(--ring, #0a0c0f); }

components.name: Secondary (Set) Button
components.description: The action vocabulary: this writes to the instrument. One step up the neutral ramp. In light mode the fill is held on hover, so the cursor and the focus ring are the affordance - the same behaviour the selected switch member has.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--secondary, #e6e9ec); color: var(--secondary-foreground, #12151a); font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: box-shadow 0.15s; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--secondary, #e6e9ec); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, #fbfcfd), 0 0 0 5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #0a0c0f) 75%, transparent); border-color: var(--ring, #0a0c0f); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: The one place the panel's chrome carries a hue. A true red where Alert is a rose, 22.27 CIEDE2000 apart in light and 15.44 in dark, so danger is never confusable with an instrument in Alert. Its focus ring is the ordinary neutral ring, and its ring gap is white rather than the surface, which makes the indicator two-tone against the fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: var(--destructive, #a3120f); color: #ffffff; font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive, #a3120f) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ffffff, 0 0 0 5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #0a0c0f) 75%, transparent); }

components.name: State Badge
components.description: The only saturated element on the panel, and the reason the chrome holds no hue. The state-to-colour mapping lives once, on a data-indi-state attribute the theme resolves to a pair of custom properties, so the badge, the status dots, the wallboard's bars and its drawn figures cannot drift apart. Busy is the only state that animates, by a ring on a pseudo-element rather than by fading the badge.
components.html: Ok Busy Alert Idle
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; position: relative; margin-right: 6px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 9999px; font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.025em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-badge-idle { background: var(--state-idle, #6b7480); color: var(--state-idle-foreground, #ffffff); } .ds-badge-ok { background: var(--state-ok, #215c1f); color: var(--state-ok-foreground, #ffffff); } .ds-badge-busy { background: var(--state-busy, #947100); color: var(--state-busy-foreground, #ffffff); } .ds-badge-alert { background: var(--state-alert, #8e0b55); color: var(--state-alert-foreground, #ffffff); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-badge[data-pulse]::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; outline: 2px solid var(--state-busy, #947100); border-radius: inherit; pointer-events: none; animation: ds-state-pulse 2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) infinite; } } @keyframes ds-state-pulse { 0% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 0.6; } 70%, 100% { transform: scale(1.5); opacity: 0; } }

components.name: Property Vector Card
components.description: The unit the panel is built from: one INDI property vector, drawn from whatever the driver declared. 16px corners, a hairline border doing the separation a shadow would elsewhere, and 16px of padding tightened from the primitive's default because a device can publish thirty of these. Its accessible name is the title and the state badge together, so it arrives as "Exposure, Alert".

components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #7c8490); border-radius: 16px; background: var(--card, #ffffff); color: var(--foreground, #12151a); box-shadow: 0px 1px 4px 0px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05), 0px 1px 2px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); } .ds-card-head { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; } .ds-card-desc { margin: 2px 0 0; font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, #434a53); } .ds-card-body { font-size: 0.875rem; }

components.name: Switch Vector Control
components.description: A fieldset of independent toggle buttons styled to look joined, and deliberately not a radio group: the ARIA radio pattern is selection-follows-focus, so arrowing would announce that the selection moved while nothing had gone on the wire. Selection is carried by weight as well as fill, because with no hue in the chrome the hovered and selected fills are adjacent steps on one neutral ramp.
components.css: .ds-switch { display: inline-flex; margin: 0; padding: 0; border: 0; } .ds-switch-member { height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid var(--input, #6d7580); border-left: 0; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, #12151a); font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-switch-member:first-child { border-left: 1px solid var(--input, #6d7580); border-top-left-radius: 10px; border-bottom-left-radius: 10px; } .ds-switch-member:last-child { border-top-right-radius: 10px; border-bottom-right-radius: 10px; } .ds-switch-member:hover { background: var(--muted, #f1f3f5); } .ds-switch-member[data-state="on"], .ds-switch-member[data-state="on"]:hover { background: var(--secondary, #e6e9ec); color: var(--secondary-foreground, #12151a); font-weight: 600; } .ds-switch-member:focus-visible { position: relative; z-index: 10; outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, #fbfcfd), 0 0 0 5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #0a0c0f) 75%, transparent); border-color: var(--ring, #0a0c0f); }

components.name: Value Input Field
components.description: Two deterministic lines per element: a header pairing the label with the live current value, then a full-width input for the requested new value underneath. Nothing competes for a single row, so a long label and a sexagesimal reading both fit. The border is the --input token, which is simultaneously this control's edge, its 30% fill in the dark schemes, and the whole of the Switch's off-state track.
components.html: 184.30
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); } .ds-field-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, #434a53); } .ds-field-value { font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size: 0.875rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 4px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--input, #6d7580); border-radius: 10px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, #12151a); font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size: 0.875rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; box-shadow: 0px 1px 4px 0px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.03); transition: box-shadow 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, #fbfcfd), 0 0 0 5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #0a0c0f) 75%, transparent); border-color: var(--ring, #0a0c0f); }

components.name: Connection Status
components.description: Two dots in the sidebar: the browser-to-bridge socket and the bridge-to-indiserver link. They differ in shape before they differ in hue - a filled disc when live, a hollow ring when not - because colour alone put the old green and red 1.08:1 apart under simulated deuteranopia. Only the failure is written out on screen; the healthy state stays visually hidden so only the alarm takes space.
components.html: bridgeindiserver offline
components.css: .ds-conn { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 4px 16px; font-family: var(--font-sans, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, #434a53); } .ds-conn-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .ds-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 2px solid transparent; } .ds-dot-on { border-color: var(--state-ok-ink, #215c1f); background: var(--state-ok-ink, #215c1f); } .ds-dot-off { border-color: var(--state-alert, #8e0b55); } .ds-conn-off { color: var(--muted-foreground, #434a53); }

components.name: Message Log Entry
components.description: A docked terminal tail: readout typeface at 0.75rem, newest at the bottom. Each entry stacks a timestamp and device name over the message body so wrapped lines start at the margin rather than mid-row. The scrolling viewport is a polite additions-only live region and carries a tab stop, without which the history above the tail is unreachable by keyboard.

components.name: Theme Control
components.description: One icon button cycling light -> dark -> night. Its label says what pressing it does, because the control is an action and "Toggle theme" stopped being true at three schemes. Grown to 44x44 for real in className rather than by an overlay, so the hover tint and the focus ring grow with the target.

components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 44px; height: 44px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, #12151a); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--accent, #e6e9ec); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background, #fbfcfd), 0 0 0 5px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, #0a0c0f) 75%, transparent); border-color: var(--ring, #0a0c0f); }

narrative.overview:
An operator is alone at 3am, a hundred miles from the instrument, and this interface is the only thing that will tell them what is happening. That is the brief. What the system does with it is narrower than "be legible": it spends its entire colour channel on one question. Colour on this surface means what an instrument is doing, and nothing else. The chrome is a neutral continuum in three renditions - light is an absorption spectrum, dark marks on a bright ground; dark is an emission spectrum, bright marks on a dark one; night is emission under a luminance ceiling - and hue appears only as narrow saturated marks at fixed positions, which are the four INDI state badges.

That is why the brand has no colour at all. --primary, --secondary and --ring are pure neutrals in all three schemes, and the wordmark separates its halves by weight rather than by hue. This is a correction, not a starting position: the palette before this one carried a violet that sat 22.4 CIEDE2000 from the nearest state colour, and the one before that an orange at 8.3. Both were the same mistake at different distances - an identity colour with a hue is a near-miss for a status colour - and removing the hue removes the class of failure instead of managing it. The only reserved non-state hue in the whole product is the documentation site's link cyan, and it never appears in the panel.

The register is instrument-grade, dense and professional, closer to a control desk than to a consumer app. Information density is a feature: the operator is an expert and slowing them down for breathing room costs them the night. The whole interface is monospace, so a column of readings aligns by default and a value never shifts as its digits change. And the palette was not chosen by eye. Nearly every colour token in theme.css carries its measured contrast ratio, composited against the real ancestor surface, plus a note on the value it replaced and why that one failed. A value is defended by measurement, and taste does not overrule a ratio.
keyCharacteristics: Three schemes, each measured independently: light (absorption), dark (emission), and night (emission under MIL-STD-1472F's 10 cd/m2 dark-adaptation ceiling).
The brand spends no chroma. Every saturated pixel on the panel is an instrument talking.
Four state hues (Idle / Ok / Busy / Alert), derived by search so every pair separates by at least 11.94 CIEDE2000 in the worst of normal, deuteranopic and protanopic vision.
Colour never carries meaning on its own: every state is written out as well as coloured.
Monospace throughout, so numeric readings align and never jitter.
Flat surfaces with visible hairline borders; four tonal surface steps do the work depth usually does.
Density over comfort. Cards are compact, the grid is tight, and the shell pins to the viewport.

rules.name: The Brand Spends No Chroma Rule
rules.body: --primary, --secondary and --ring are neutrals in all three schemes, so hue on the panel only ever means instrument state. A new accent does not get measured against the state colours and admitted if it is far enough away; it does not get a hue at all. The one reserved non-state hue in the product is the documentation site's link cyan, and it never appears in the panel.

rules.name: The Measured Value Rule
rules.body: A colour token clears its bar on every surface it is used over, not on the lightest one, and the bar is AAA wherever AAA is arithmetically reachable. Two tokens clear their bar by under 10% and each carries a re-measure note in theme.css beside the value: --input against its own bg-input/30 fill, at 3.19 light and 3.25 dark.

rules.name: The Fill Is Frozen Rule
rules.body: The four state fills are tuned for separation from each other, so contrast is fixed on the foreground and never on the fill. Compressing a fill down the lightness axis to carry a darker label is exactly what collapsed the previous set to CIEDE2000 2.3. Four of the twelve state badges cannot reach AAA at any foreground, and that is recorded rather than smoothed.

rules.name: The One Reserved Line Rule
rules.body: Exactly one non-state hue exists in the product, it is the documentation site's link cyan, and it lives on the docs site only. The panel and the docs share the header colour, the ground and the type; the cyan is the one thing that does not cross.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that updates while the operator is looking at it is set in tabular figures. Telemetry arrives continuously, and proportional digits make a stable reading appear to twitch, which reads as instability in the instrument rather than in the font.

rules.name: The Label Is Not The Name Rule
rules.body: Human-facing text always comes from the display label helper, never from the raw INDI name. Wire names appear in exactly one place, the debug detail line under a card title, and only when the operator has asked for them.

rules.name: The Wordmark Separates By Weight Rule
rules.body: "INDI" is 400 and "kit" is 700, and neither half is coloured. A coloured wordmark would be the single exception to the rule that hue means instrument state - in the corner of every page.

rules.name: The Container Query Rule
rules.body: Column counts are measured from the container, never the viewport. Any component that can sit beside a docked panel counts its own width.

rules.name: The Heading Chain Rule
rules.body: The outline is shell h1, group h2, card title h3, with no step skipped. A property group that carries no name still emits a visually hidden h2, because dropping it would step h1 straight to h3 and break the outline that is the only fast way to navigate thirty cards without a mouse.

rules.name: The Docked Strip Pays For Itself Rule
rules.body: A strip that shares the viewport with the instrument grid sizes to its content (h-auto max-h-56), never to a fixed height. A fixed 224px charged the grid whether the log held two lines or two hundred, and the cut landed mid-outline.

rules.name: The Pill Means Readout Rule
rules.body: Fully round is reserved for things that report and cannot be pressed - state badges, status dots, the unread count. Anything an operator can act on carries the 10px control radius. Never round a control to a pill; it reads as a status.

rules.name: The Shape Carries The State Rule
rules.body: Where a mark is the whole object, it differs in shape before it differs in hue. The connection dots are a filled disc when live and a hollow ring when not; the wallboard's three shutter readings are three shapes.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every state is written out in text as well as coloured: the badge carries its own name, and the status dot is decorative and marked hidden because its label sits beside it. This holds independently of how well the states separate.

rules.name: The Ring Stands Off The Control Rule
rules.body: A focus ring is measured against both its neighbours, not just the surface. With a neutral ring on a neutral primary the ring and the fill are nearly the same value - 1.06:1 light, 1.20:1 dark, 1.00:1 on destructive - so removing the brand's hue made this worse, not better, and the 2px offset is not optional.

rules.name: The Registry Is Corrected In CSS, Not In Place Rule
rules.body: The shadcn primitives stay registry-exact and are overruled from theme.css by rules outside every @layer, hooked on the utility class the registry emits rather than on data-slot, which does not survive asChild. An unlayered rule setting a real property beats every state variant, so it must restate them or be narrowed to something that cannot be in them.

rules.name: The Target Is Bigger Than The Control Rule
rules.body: Every interactive target is 44x44. Where the app composes the control it grows for real, so the feedback grows with the target; where the box belongs to a primitive the theme adds a transparent ::before overlay. The overlay grows the target but not the feedback, and the controls still at 32px are enumerated rather than hidden.

dos: Do keep the chrome neutral. --primary, --secondary and --ring hold no chroma, so every saturated pixel on the panel is an instrument reporting its state.
Do re-measure a colour on every surface it appears over before changing it, and leave the measured ratio in a comment beside the value, as every existing token does.
Do write every state out in text as well as colouring it, in text a sighted reader can see, and give a bare mark a shape as well as a hue.
Do use tabular figures for anything numeric that updates live.
Do reach for a hairline border or one of the four surface tones when you need separation.
Do count grid columns from the container's width, using container queries.
Do keep the heading chain unbroken (h1 -> h2 -> h3), emitting a visually hidden heading rather than skipping a level.

Do give every control the same 10px radius and the same 3px focus ring at 75% opacity, held 2px off the control so it never touches its own fill, and let the border shift beside it stand - focus is two signals, never one.
Do correct a vendored primitive from theme.css, unlayered and hooked on the utility class it emits, rather than by editing src/ui/.
Do grow fixed edges by their safe-area inset, and remember the underscore spacing Tailwind needs inside calc() around env().
Do apply .night alongside .dark, never instead of it.
Do keep the panel and the documentation on the same neutral identity; they are one product and the values are shared deliberately.
donts: Don't give the brand a hue, however far it measures from the four states. The distance is not the rule; the absence is.
Don't adjust a --state-* fill to fix a contrast problem. Change the foreground, and record the shortfall where the ceiling makes AAA unreachable.

Don't chase the night scheme's luminance ceiling with dim greys. The cap is met by a black ground and the operator's own brightness control; dimming the colours loses the contrast and still misses the ceiling by more than tenfold.
Don't animate by fading opacity on anything carrying text. Fading a badge to 0.5 measured 1.75:1, and no fill colour survives it. Move the motion to a pseudo-element instead.

Don't write an unlayered rule that sets a real property - border-color, position, background-color - without restating every state that property can be in, or narrowing the selector to something that cannot be in them. Custom properties are the safe case.
Don't turn the switch control back into a radio group, or let an unselected member reach the selected member's appearance on hover.
Don't round a control to a pill or square off a badge; the two shapes carry the pressable/reportable distinction.
Don't put the documentation's link cyan on the panel, or add a second reserved hue anywhere.
Don't turn this into a data-visualisation dashboard. Wall-to-wall charts, sparklines on every reading and neon series colours on near-black are the confirmed anti-reference.
Don't cite the shadow scale as evidence of an elevation philosophy. It is inherited and its purpose is undecided.
Don't put colour in an architecture diagram. Those render on GitHub and the docs site in every scheme, and a hardcoded palette becomes unreadable in one of them.
